pull.title: Keep witness stacks in serialized form in CScriptWitness
pull.body:
This is split off from #36521. This PR focuses on reducing memory usage of transactions in memory, leaving performance improvements for other PRs.

`CScriptWitness` stores a witness stack as a `std::vector<std::vector<unsigned char>>`, which costs a 24-byte vector object and an allocation for every non-empty element. This makes it possible to construct transactions that take a large amount of memory after deserialization.

This PR first introduces encapsulation for `CScriptWitness`, hiding its representation. The last commit then changes the representation to be single `std::unique_ptr<byte[]>` which for non-empty witness stacks stores their serialization prefixed by a small length header. Witnesses can no longer be modified in place; they can only be replaced in their entirety. Access to the individual witness stack elements is done by on-the-fly deserialization instead.

`CScriptWitness` shrinks from 24 to 8 bytes, and `CTxIn` from 112 to 96 bytes. Worst-case allocated size for transactions kept in memory drops from roughly 28 bytes/WU to 1.6 bytes/WU.

This worsens deserialization and validation time, adding some 50-70 ms per block to the worst case for me. A follow-up #36918 with optimizations improves the worst case deserialization time significantly instead. Other minor degradations:
* libbitcoinkernel's witness stack element accessor becomes $\mathcal{O}(n)$ in the index of the witness element; using it to iterate a whole witness may therefore become $\mathcal{O}(n^2)$.
* `CScriptWitness::back()` is $\mathcal{O}(n)$ in the length of the witness stack.

Issue reported by furszy and 0xB10C.

events.message:
script: give CScriptWitness an interface that hides its representation

Add element access through spans (forward iteration, front(), back(), and
indexing), conversion to and construction from a vector of elements,
serialization, and memory usage accounting, so that users no longer need to
access the stack vector directly. This prepares for a future commit which
will replace the representation with a more compact & efficient one.

The stack vector itself stays public until the next commits have converted
its users.

test: check CScriptWitness against the vector of vectors it represents

Add a unit test and a fuzz test that compare CScriptWitness's interface
(accessors, construction, and serialization) with the
std::vector<std::vector<unsigned char>> it represents. The unit test
focuses on element counts and sizes around CompactSize encoding
boundaries.

scripted-diff: use CScriptWitness's size(), empty() and back()

Convert the uses of CScriptWitness::stack that only need the number of
elements, whether there are any, or the last element, which the witness
provides itself. Other uses are converted in the next commits.

-BEGIN VERIFY SCRIPT-
# Lines that need the stack itself (to compute the size of its
# serialization without the element count, to pass the last element
# where a vector is expected, or to index all elements in a loop) are
# left for the manual changes.
sed -i -E -e '/GetSizeOfCompactSize|TAPROOT_LEAF_TAPSCRIPT|i < (txin\.)?scriptWitness\.stack/b' \
    -e 's/\.stack\.(size|empty|back)\(\)/.\1()/g' \
    $(git grep -l -E '\.stack\.(size|empty|back)\(\)' -- src ':!src/script/miniscript.*' ':!src/script/script.h')
-END VERIFY SCRIPT-

scripted-diff: read and compare CScriptWitness through its interface

Convert the uses of CScriptWitness::stack that read an element by index,
bind a const reference to the stack, or compare two stacks, and the
uses of IsNull().

-BEGIN VERIFY SCRIPT-
FILES=$(git grep -l -E '\.stack\b' -- src ':!src/script/miniscript.*' ':!src/script/script.h')

# Reading an element by index: the witness has operator[] itself. Writes
# to elements, and loops indexing all elements (which can be quadratic
# with indexing that is not constant-time), are left for the manual
# changes.
sed -i -E -e '/MAX_STANDARD_P2WSH_STACK_ITEM_SIZE|HexStr\((txin\.)?scriptWitness\.stack\[|\.stack\[[^]]*\]( =|\.resize)|^\s*\+\+/b' \
    -e 's/\.stack\[/[/g' $FILES

# Const references to the stack: refer to the witness itself, which
# provides the same read-only accessors.
sed -i -E 's/^(\s*const auto& \w+( = |\{).*)\.stack(\}?;)$/\1\3/' $FILES

# Comparisons of two stacks: compare the witnesses, which are equal
# exactly when their stacks are.
sed -i -E '/\.stack [!=]= /s/\.stack\b//g' $FILES

# IsNull(): use empty(), which the witness provides along with size()
# and its other container-like accessors.
sed -i -E -e 's/(scriptWitness|final_script_witness)\.IsNull\(\)/\1.empty()/g' \
    -e 's/witness->IsNull\(\)/witness->empty()/g' \
    $(git grep -l -E '(scriptWitness|final_script_witness)\.IsNull\(\)|witness->IsNull\(\)' -- src)
-END VERIFY SCRIPT-

scripted-diff: serialize CScriptWitness rather than its stack

Convert the uses of CScriptWitness::stack that serialize or deserialize
it, or compute the size of its serialization. The witness itself has the
same serialization as its stack.

-BEGIN VERIFY SCRIPT-
sed -i -E -e 's/ (>>|<<) ([][A-Za-z0-9_.]+)\.stack( <<|;)/ \1 \2\3/' \
    -e 's/(SerializeToVector|UnserializeFromVector)\(s, (\w+)\.stack\)/\1(s, \2)/' \
    -e 's/::GetSerializeSize\(([][A-Za-z0-9_.]+)\.stack\)/::GetSerializeSize(\1)/' \
    $(git grep -l -E '\.stack\b' -- src ':!src/script/miniscript.*' ':!src/script/script.h')
-END VERIFY SCRIPT-

scripted-diff: replace witnesses as a whole instead of their stack

Convert the uses of CScriptWitness::stack (and SetNull()) that clear the
stack, assign a new one, or push a single element onto an empty one, to
assigning a new witness. The remaining uses are converted manually in
the next commits.

-BEGIN VERIFY SCRIPT-
FILES=$(git grep -l -E '\.stack\b|(scriptWitness|final_script_witness)\.SetNull\(\)' -- src ':!src/script/miniscript.*' ':!src/script/script.h')

# Clearing the stack (SetNull(), clear() or resize(0)): assign an empty
# witness. A clear() followed by pushing elements in a loop is left for
# the manual changes.
sed -i -E -e '/txin\.scriptWitness\.stack\.clear/b' \
    -e 's/(scriptWitness|final_script_witness)\.SetNull\(\)/\1 = {}/' \
    -e 's/(scriptWitness)\.stack\.(clear\(\)|resize\(0\));$/\1 = {};/' $FILES

# Assigning a vector of elements to the stack: assign a witness
# constructed from it (moving from the vector is pointless, as the
# witness is constructed from a const reference). An assignment that
# spells out the vector's type is left for the manual changes.
sed -i -E -e '/\.stack = std::vector</b' \
    -e 's/(\w+)\.stack = (std::move\((\w+)\)|(.*));$/\1 = CScriptWitness{\3\4};/' $FILES

# Pushing a single element onto an empty witness (in these benchmarks
# and tests): assign a witness constructed from that element. The one
# place that pushes onto a non-empty witness (to make a different
# witness) is left for the manual changes, as are pushes in loops.
sed -i -E '/ tx\.vin\[0\]\.scriptWitness\.stack\.push_back\(\{5\}\)|Consume/!s/(\w+)\.stack\.push_back\((.*)\);$/\1 = CScriptWitness{{\2}};/' \
    src/bench/blockencodings.cpp src/bench/mempool_eviction.cpp src/bench/mempool_stress.cpp src/bench/rpc_mempool.cpp \
    src/test/fuzz/connect_block.cpp src/test/fuzz/txdownloadman.cpp src/test/orphanage_tests.cpp src/test/txdownload_tests.cpp \
    src/test/validation_block_tests.cpp
-END VERIFY SCRIPT-

script: let ExecuteWitnessScript take its initial stack by value

This lets callers move the stack into it, rather than having it be
copied from a span. This will be used in a future commit.

script: build the witness execution stack with ToVectors()

VerifyWitnessProgram used a span over CScriptWitness::stack, popped the
elements with other roles (the witness script, the annex, the control
block, and the leaf script) off that span, and copied the remaining
elements into the initial execution stack.

Instead, convert the witness to a vector of vectors once, using
ToVectors(), pop those elements off that vector, and move what remains
into the execution stack.

refactor: use CScriptWitness's interface where that needs more than a rename

Convert the remaining non-test uses of CScriptWitness::stack, which need
more than a substitution.

This includes the range-based for loops over the stack. Iterating over a
CScriptWitness yields its elements as spans, by value, where the stack's
elements were vectors bound by reference. The spans refer to memory
owned by the witness, so they stay valid as long as it is not modified.

test, bench, fuzz: build witness stacks before constructing a CScriptWitness

Convert the remaining uses of CScriptWitness::stack in tests, benchmarks,
and fuzz tests, by constructing witnesses from a separately-built vector
of elements, rather than modifying the stack in place.

script: remove CScriptWitness's old interface

All users of CScriptWitness now go through the interface that hides its
representation. Make the stack vector private, turning the struct into a
class, and remove IsNull() and SetNull(), which have no callers left.

The representation itself does not change here.

span: add SameSpan

Add a helper that tells whether two spans refer to the same range of
memory, rather than whether their contents are equal. A future commit
uses it to compare iterators that consist of a span.

This should be able to be addressed by an API function that walks the stack once and hands each item's bytes to the caller. Testing it out.

Edit: See: #36909

Did another clanker deep dive to see its performance effects on memory and  verification speed. On the historical blockchain it seems like noise. Under adversarial conditions slightly slower verification speeds when dealing with related issues, but nothing remotely close to close to worst case blocks, even post-bip54. 

Worst case regression I'm getting is +149ms for a block that is just 4M of witness data elements, which is a bit north of "50-70 ms per block" but might be due to measurement differences, and is largely irrelevant anyways.

Can share longer form slop on request, but nothing concerning.

@instagibbs FWIW, these are the benchmarks I based this on. "minimal" is this PR. The "lazy conversion" and "direction deserialization" are follow-up optimizations not included in this PR. Hardware is a high-end Zen5 machine.

---

Each row is one 4M WU block, timed over deserialize, `CheckBlock` and `ConnectBlock`, in ms. These are medians of 11 interleaved rounds on the now-idle machine, gcc Release.

| block | master | minimal | + lazy conversion | + direct deserialization |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| valid: unknown witness version, 2M one-byte items | 99 | 169 (+70) | 108 | 76 |
| invalid: P2WPKH with 2M one-byte items | 99 | 169 (+70) | 108 | 77 |
| valid: unknown tapleaf version, 2M one-byte items | 99 | 151 (+52) | 151 | 70 |
| invalid: P2WSH script mismatch, 2M one-byte items | 99 | 147 (+48) | 147 | 66 |
| invalid: P2WSH script mismatch, 4M empty items | 249 | 293 (+44) | 294 | 59 |
| invalid: P2WSH with 4M empty items (master's slowest) | 307 | 296 (−11) | 294 | 61 |
| valid: 5,169 P2WSH spends of 403 items | 22.2 | 23.3 (+1.1) | 23.4 | 21.8 |

crACK a6a4df2770eb5f79f4e2dc58dee12889ca0be700

This change reduces the memory usage of `CScriptWitness`. Instead of the parsed representation it stores the serialized version. Memory footprint is reduced especially for empty witnesses, or for empty or small witness elements. Considering that the parsing is relatively low complexity, and the usage pattern, the tradeoff seems to be worth it.

Instead of storing a byte vector (with a footprint of 3 values, 24 bytes on 64-bit systems) it pushes the optimization further: it stores a byte pointer, no allocated size / capacity, and the length in 4 bytes inside the data buffer. The memory needed for the fields is thus 8 bytes inline plus 4 extra bytes on the heap, but only for non-empty witnesses.

The commits are granular and well structured (nice usage of scripted diffs for usage switch).

Two minor issues left as comments. No other issues found.

An alternative considered: Store the length as a separate field, not part of the buffer. The advantages would be: simpler access to the serialized form, and no header read on each access. However, the memory usage improvement -- the biggest win of this PR -- would take a hit (8 extra bytes for every witness, including empty ones; `CTxIn` size from 96 to 104).

A note on the range of counts and lengths: `uint64_t ReadCompactSize()` is implicitly converted to `size_t` in a few places. This is fine: `ReadCompactSize` rejects values above `MAX_SIZE` (2^25), so anything it returns fits in 26 bits. For deserialized witnesses this always holds; for witnesses built from vectors it holds in practice. It's worth mentioning that it's possible to construct an artificially large witness with an element larger than `MAX_SIZE`. In this case `std::terminate` would be hit on first access, since the accessors are noexcept. That's not reachable from the network, but checking `MAX_SIZE` in the constructor would make the invariant hold by construction.

Further (followup) ideas:

- I wonder if this "light read-only byte vector" construct would be worthwhile to be separated on its own into utils.

- A potential optimization: Since the class wrote the serialization itself, lengths can be decoded without `ReadCompactSize`'s internal checks, with a fast path for one-byte lengths. This also removes the terminate case above, as decoding can no longer throw. In addition, `operator[]` can read the header and the element count only once instead of twice. In a quick micro-benchmark this made iteration, `back()` and `[]` on a typical 3-element witness about 5× faster, and 1.4–2× faster for 10k one-byte elements; see [branch pr36895-oo-optim1](https://github.com/optout21/bitcoin/tree/pr36895-oo-optim1).

events.message:
script: store witness stacks as their serialization

Replace CScriptWitness's vector of vectors with a single allocation,
containing the size of the stack's serialization (4 bytes, little
endian), followed by that serialization. An empty stack uses no
allocation at all.

This means a witness stack no longer needs one allocation per non-empty
element plus one for the outer vector, and no longer has a 24-byte
overhead per element. A block whose witnesses consist of millions of
tiny elements thus no longer costs tens of bytes of memory and an
allocation per byte. It also shrinks CScriptWitness from 24 to 8 bytes,
and thus CTxIn from 112 to 96 bytes. The downside is that indexing
becomes O(n) in the distance from the bottom of the stack.

This is the simplest implementation of this representation:
deserialization still goes through a vector of vectors, and elements
are found by parsing the serialization with SpanReader and
ReadCompactSize. Both can be made faster in follow-up changes.

events.body:
> * A potential optimization: Since the class wrote the serialization itself, lengths can be decoded without `ReadCompactSize`'s internal checks, with a fast path for one-byte lengths.

I like this, a natural consequence of this is that it would speed up the kernel.

ACK https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36895/commits/0c981e75a9e7e352d1c0f08118596ea91a9fa102

Ran quite a few validation passes over worst-case at-rest memory usage for various places like orphanage and other vectors. Does what it says on the tin with no slowdown on average case transaction/block patterns, the biggest exception being single transaction NFT blocks which are a few hundred mics slower due to double copying of the exec_script.

Also, looks like mempool will fit ~13-15% more transactions in it, based on my historical simulations.

This change also doesn't seem make future updates to interface any more difficult, so we're not being boxed in with this bugfix change.

CI failures seem unrelated

@optout21 I had a series of several optimizations in my old PR #36521, some of which do similar things to what you suggest. I've opened a draft PR #36918 with those optimization to avoid duplicate work.

This PR is deliberately avoiding performance optimizations, to focus review on the more important issue of memory usage.

---

> An alternative considered: Store the length as a separate field, not part of the buffer. The advantages would be: simpler access to the serialized form, and no header read on each access. However, the memory usage improvement -- the biggest win of this PR -- would take a hit (8 extra bytes for every witness, including empty ones; CTxIn size from 96 to 104).

I'd rather not do that. Memory usage is the priority here I think. In the follow-up PR the header is also expanded with the position of the last element, so that `CScriptWitness::back()` runs is $\mathcal{O}(1)$ time.

> In this case std::terminate would be hit on first access, since the accessors are noexcept. That's not reachable from the network, but checking MAX_SIZE in the constructor would make the invariant hold by construction.

The follow-up uses an optimized decoder that never throws (but relies on the fact that the bytes are self-encoded and thus guaranteed to be correct).

> I wonder if this "light read-only byte vector" construct would be worthwhile to be separated on its own into utils.

If there is a second use case for it, that seems reasonable, but I'm not sure where that'd be.

> Since the class wrote the serialization itself, lengths can be decoded without ReadCompactSize's internal checks, with a fast path for one-byte lengths.

I believe the old PR already had that; it's in the follow-up PR now.

comments.body:
> [a6a4df2](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36895/changes/a6a4df2770eb5f79f4e2dc58dee12889ca0be700) _script: store witness stacks as their serialization_:

Nit: Could be simplified to: (requires `#include <util/string.h>`)
```
    return "CScriptWitness(" + util::Join(*this, ", ", [](auto element) { return HexStr(element); }) + ")";
```

> [0a82e05](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36895/changes/0a82e05e34b920c7400f945a830b120f99a7e9d8) _refactor: use CScriptWitness's interface where that needs more than a rename_:

Minor: Here `back()` is called, then `ToSpans()`. If the `MAX_STANDARD_P2WSH_SCRIPT_SIZE` check was moved after `ToSpans()`, the `back()` call could be avoided (`back` is potentially expensive).
#36918 instead has a lazy creation of the stack (and no more `ToSpans`), which avoids this issue entirely I think.
